headline: Tora is “anomalous”: Old Japanese to₁ra where the expected form was *tura.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese to₁ra, from Proto-Japonic *tora.

Pellard (2013, 92) includes to₁ra among words with o₁ excepted from the /-o-/ to /-u-/ vowel-raising rule and not originating from earlier diphthongs. According to Vovin (2021, 111), West Old Japanese *to₁ra, instead of expected *tura, is "anomalous" and possibly "a case of a sporadic analogical development".
Vovin (2013) asserts that this word is same as a Silla place name 刀良 (/*tora/), which matches the Old Japanese phonographic spelling.

sources.quote: Sino-Japanese compound of 太 (tai, “big, fat, thick”) + 鼓 (ko, “drum”).

headline: Wakareru is from Old Japanese wakaru, and cognate with 分かれる (wakareru) and 分ける (wakeru).

sources.quote: From Old Japanese わかる (wakaru), in the 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) pattern. Cognate with 分(わ)かれる (wakareru) and 分(わ)ける (wakeru).
Development

Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

sources.quote: From 生 (nama-, “raw → inexperienced, saucy”) + 意気 (iki, “spirit”).

sources.quote: 収(しゅう) (shū, “take possession of”) + 入(にゅう) (nyū, “enter, go in, come in”).

headline: Ka, “mosquito”, may be related to 噛む (kamu, “to bite”) or 痒い (kayui, “itchy”), but the ultimate derivation remains unknown.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese. Possibly related to 噛む (kamu, “to bite”) or 痒い (kayui, “itchy”), although the ultimate derivation remains unknown.

headline: Nemui is related to 眠る (nemuru, “to sleep”), all ultimately related to Classical Japanese 寝 (nu, “to sleep”).

sources.quote: Compare 眠る (nemuru, “to sleep”), 眠り (nemuri, “sleep”), 眠たい (nemutai, “sleepy”), and おねむ (o-nemu, “(childish) sleepiness, sleep”), all ultimately related to Classical Japanese 寝 (nu, “to sleep”, modern 寝る (neru)).

sources.quote: 大(だい) (dai-, “great”) + 統領(とうりょう) (tōryō, “leader”)

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 情 (MC dzjeng).
